text.p: Two goals from Norway's Steffen Iverson on Saint Stephen's Day and a third from Dane Alan Neilsen gave Tottenham Hotspur a 3-1 win over Southampton in the English premier league on Thursday.

Iverson, who joined Spurs earlier this month after helping Rosenborg Trondheim into the European Cup quarter-finals, scored his debut goal for the Londoners inside the first minute, bundling the ball home after Southampton goalkeeper Dave Beasant had parried a David Howells shot.
The Norwegian added his second in similar circumstances. Teddy Sheringham put Andy Sinton through on goal, his lob was palmed out by Beasant and Iverson was on hand to slide the ball into the net.

England midfielder Matthew Le Tissier came off the substitutes' banch to pull a goal back for the visitors before halftime but Neilsen sealed a confidence-boosting victory for Spurs with a headed goal from a free kick in the 63rd minute.

Southampton, with the worst away record in the premier league, were unlucky not to come away with a point after twice hitting the woodwork in the first half. They remain fifth from bottom and face a difficult visit to Liverpool on Saturday.
Spurs, who play Newcastle at the weekend, move into eighth place, level on points with Chelsea and Everton, both in action when eight other premier league games are played later in the day.
